title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 211 (Establishment of Serious Fraud Investigation Office)

content.overview: Section 211 establishes the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) to investigate frauds relating to a company. The office is headed by a Director and consists of experts from fields such as banking, corporate affairs, taxation, forensic audit, capital market, information technology, law and other fields as the Central Government may prescribe. Assignment of a particular company’s investigation to SFIO is under section 212. Section 211 creates the institutional office; it does not itself open an investigation into any company.
content.glance: SFIO established to investigate company-related frauds; headed by a Director; multi-disciplinary experts; assignment of cases is s. 212 — s. 211 only creates the office.
content.study: The Central Government shall establish an office to be called the Serious Fraud Investigation Office to investigate frauds relating to a company. The SFIO shall be headed by a Director and consist of such number of experts from the fields of banking, corporate affairs, taxation, forensic audit, capital market, information technology, law or such other fields as the Central Government may prescribe. Current-law framing: identify SFIO as the statutory office for investigating company frauds; note composition and leadership; reserve the power to assign a case for investigation to section 212. Do not treat s. 211 as an investigation order.

sections.heading: Establishment
sections.body: Central Government establishes the Serious Fraud Investigation Office to investigate frauds relating to a company.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.body: Headed by a Director; consists of experts from banking, corporate affairs, taxation, forensic audit, capital market, IT, law and other prescribed fields.

sections.heading: Relationship to Assignment
sections.body: s. 211 creates the office; assignment of a particular investigation is under section 212.

provisions.title: Establishment of Serious Fraud Investigation Office

examples.title: Office vs case assignment
examples.body: A complainant demands that ‘SFIO investigate under section 211’. Section 211 establishes the office. Assignment of a company’s affairs to SFIO for investigation is a Central Government decision under section 212.

examples.title: Multi-disciplinary composition
examples.body: SFIO is staffed with experts from forensic audit, capital market and law among other fields, reflecting the complex nature of corporate fraud investigations under s. 211.

hypotheticals.question: Does the existence of SFIO under s. 211 mean every corporate fraud is automatically investigated by SFIO?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 211 establishes the office. Whether a particular company’s affairs are assigned to SFIO is governed by section 212 and the Central Government’s decision on the grounds stated there.

distinctions.title: SFIO establishment (s. 211) vs SFIO investigation (s. 212)
distinctions.left: Creates the office and its composition
distinctions.right: Assigns investigation of a company’s affairs to SFIO

misconceptions.trap: Section 211 itself orders investigation of any named company by SFIO.
misconceptions.correction: Section 211 only establishes SFIO. Assignment of investigation of a company’s affairs is under section 212.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 211 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify SFIO as statutory office. II. Note composition. III. Distinguish assignment under s. 212. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Office facts; composition; assignment status under s. 212; precise relief.
